Two-axis taxonomy (BLOCKING / NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE / SUGGESTION ×
factual / structural / scope).

This instance SATURATES top_k at 5/5 — the 6th category to fully clear.
The instance pattern mirrors the just-locked worlds_largest_container_ports_by_2024_teu
(top_k + time-series-master-wins canonical-source rule).

Pay attention to:

(1) **Canonical-source rule application for time-series Passengers** —
    same master-wins inversion as the ports instance. Verify each of the
    6 per-airport articles flagged with stale body figures (Hartsfield–Jackson
    108.1M-2024-body / Guangzhou 63.1M-2023-body / Shenzhen Bao'an 52.7M-2023-body
    / LA 76.59M-2024-body / KUL 57.08M-2024-body / DFW 81.76M-2023-body)
    is resolved via master-wins.

(2) Universe rule honesty — does source_defined + table_title + db_analog
    + temporal_note coherently describe the "top-20 by 2025 passenger
    traffic per Wikipedia master article" universe? The master is using
    2025 as the current year (ACI sourced); confirm.

(3) Source verification — for each of the 20 staged rows, confirm:
    - Wikipedia master article 2025 column has the staged value
    - Per-airport article exists and supplies the staged Country + City
    - 4 master-vs-per-article name differences resolved per Wikipedia
      article title (Haneda Airport, O'Hare International Airport,
      Singapore Changi Airport, Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport)

(4) Istanbul Region = Europe — per master grouping. Verify the master
    article ranks Istanbul under European regional groupings. Alternative
    Middle East reading documented as open_question.

(5) Indira Gandhi 2025 figure is Indian fiscal year Apr-2024 to Mar-2025
    (not strict calendar 2025). Verify master treats it as the 2025 row.

(6) Diacritics + special characters: en-dash in Hartsfield–Jackson and
    Madrid–Barajas; acute á in Adolfo Suárez; ASCII apostrophe in
    Bao'an + O'Hare; slash in Dallas/Fort Worth.

(7) City conventions:
    - Haneda → 'Tokyo' (primary city; Ōta is sub-ward)
    - Dallas/Fort Worth → 'Dallas/Fort Worth' (dual-city per airport name)
    - Schiphol → 'Haarlemmermeer' (per infobox; ports precedent for
      precise municipality over canonical association)
    - KUL → 'Sepang' (per infobox)

(8) Sort order: Passengers DESC + Airport ASC alphabetical secondary.
    No exact ties in staged 20 (closest is Heathrow 84.5 vs Istanbul 84.4).

(9) Entity-class classification: `engineered-structures/airports`
    (NEW fine-class) — bucket extends from 3 to 4 instances after this
    Ready (bridges + buildings + dams + airports). Verify this classification
    is consistent with the policy.

Return condensed verdict block. Append findings to
worlds_busiest_airports_by_passenger_traffic.comments.json.

Registration-readiness sweep: Ready with hygiene — 0 blocking issues.

Verdict: Ready, but not clean. Counts by severity: 0 BLOCKING, 3 NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE, 0 SUGGESTION. Counts by issue type: factual 1, structural 2, scope-related 0.

Findings:

H1. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) decision_log Rule 6 has a stale/contradictory city-count sentence.
Evidence: the staged CSV has 20 rows and 20 distinct City values: Atlanta, Dubai, Tokyo, Dallas/Fort Worth, Shanghai, Chicago, London, Istanbul, Guangzhou, Denver, Delhi, Incheon, Los Angeles, Paris, Beijing, Singapore, Haarlemmermeer, Madrid, Shenzhen, Sepang. curation.json::decision_log Rule 6 says "19 distinct cities" and then says the 20-row CSV has 20 unique City values. curation.json::normalization_decisions already has the correct 20-distinct-city wording.
Minimal fix: change decision_log Rule 6 to "20 distinct cities (one per airport; Singapore appears as both Country and City as a city-state)" and keep the existing city-convention examples.

H2. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) The "4 master-vs-per-article name differences" count overstates the actual differences by including Singapore Changi, which is not a difference.
Evidence: Wikipedia master article 2025 statistics row 16 lists "Singapore Changi Airport"; the per-airport article title/source URL is also Singapore Changi Airport. Active narrative in draft._extraction_notes, decision_log R4/Rule 4, normalization_decisions, and open_questions item 9 says there are 4 master-vs-per-article name differences and lists Singapore Changi as one of them while also marking it "concur" in some places.
Minimal fix: rewrite as "3 master-vs-per-article name differences (Haneda, O'Hare, Dallas/Fort Worth), plus Singapore Changi as a checked concurrence." No CSV change needed.

H3. (factual, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) open_questions item 1 overgeneralizes the 2025 section as full-calendar-year despite the documented Indira Gandhi fiscal-year exception.
Evidence: the master article includes Indira Gandhi International Airport in the 2025 statistics section at 79,259,890 passengers, and the Indira Gandhi per-airport article's statistics box labels that figure as April 2024 – March 2025. source_coverage_notes and open_questions item 4 correctly document the fiscal-year exception, but open_questions item 1 says the 2025 section is "full-calendar-year 2025" without caveat.
Minimal fix: soften open_questions item 1 to "master article's most-recent section is 2025 statistics (ACI sourced; mostly annual/current-year figures, with the Indira Gandhi fiscal-year exception documented in item 4)" or simply remove "full-calendar-year".

Passed checks:
- Universe rule: source_defined + table_title + db_analog + temporal_note coherently describe the top-20 airports by 2025 passenger traffic per Wikipedia's List of busiest airports by passenger traffic master article. The master article explicitly has a 2025 statistics section and states ACI annual figures are used for consistency.
- Passenger values: all 20 staged values match the master article's 2025 passenger column after converting to millions and rounding to one decimal: ATL 106.3, DXB 95.2, Haneda 91.7, DFW 85.7, Shanghai Pudong 85.0, O'Hare 84.8, Heathrow 84.5, Istanbul 84.4, Guangzhou 83.6, Denver 82.4, Indira Gandhi 79.3, Incheon 74.1, LAX 73.7, CDG 72.0, Beijing Capital 70.7, Changi 70.0, Schiphol 68.8, Madrid-Barajas 68.2, Shenzhen Bao'an 66.5, KUL 63.3.
- Canonical-source rule: the time-series master-wins rule is honestly documented in temporal_note, source_coverage_notes, and decision_log Rule 2. It does not contradict bridges/dams because those used static structural metrics while airport passengers are annual throughput data.
- Stale per-airport figures are handled consistently by master-wins: Hartsfield-Jackson 2024 body 108.1M vs 2025 master 106.3M; Guangzhou 2023 body 63.1M vs 83.6M; Shenzhen Bao'an 2023 body 52.7M vs 66.5M; LAX 2024 body 76.59M vs 73.7M; KUL 2024 body 57.08M vs 63.3M; DFW 2023 body 81.76M vs 85.7M.
- Per-airport source support: cited per-airport articles exist and support the staged Country/City for the checked rows, including Haneda/Tokyo, DFW/Dallas-Fort Worth, Schiphol/Haarlemmermeer, KUL/Sepang, Istanbul/Istanbul, and Atlanta/United States/Atlanta. The remaining rows align with the master/per-airport Roles block.
- Istanbul Region = Europe is defensible: Istanbul Airport page locates it on the European side of Istanbul and describes it as among Europe's busiest; the master article's regional counts are consistent with treating European-side Istanbul as Europe while Asian-side Sabiha Gokcen would fall outside that row's framing.
- Indira Gandhi fiscal-year handling is correctly documented in source_coverage_notes/open_questions item 4 and the master still treats the figure as row 11 in the 2025 statistics section.
- Special-character normalization passes: Hartsfield–Jackson and Madrid–Barajas use en-dashes; Adolfo Suárez preserves acute á; Bao'an and O'Hare use ASCII apostrophes; Dallas/Fort Worth uses slash per article title.
- Sort order passes: Passengers DESC then Airport ASC; no exact ties in staged 20.
- Entity-class classification as engineered-structures/airports is consistent with the inventory policy: the PK is a named built physical structure/infrastructure entity, and airports are a new fine-class under the engineered-structures bucket.
- Source discovery: the current master article, List of busiest airports by passenger traffic, is the direct Wiki-family universe/ranking source. No stronger Wikipedia universe source is needed for this staged scope.

Minimal fixes needed:
1. decision_log Rule 6: 19 distinct cities -> 20 distinct cities.
2. Replace "4 master-vs-per-article name differences" with "3 differences + Singapore Changi concurrence" across draft._extraction_notes, decision_log, normalization_decisions, and open_questions.
3. Remove or qualify "full-calendar-year 2025" in open_questions item 1 to account for the Indira Gandhi fiscal-year exception.
